$description: Type ROLES — what a piece of text is, pointing at the sizes in type-scale.json. Decided 2026-09-22 (Ben) to close the open question in canon/design/patterns/titles-and-labels.md: the four styles were rules in prose and sizes in code, so each lane picked by eye. A role never carries its own number; changing the scale changes every role with it.

role-screen-title.$description: The title of any screen that holds a list, a form, a step or a record. Semibold, primary ink (titles-and-labels 1).

role-statement.$description: A one-thing screen whose title IS the content: an outcome, a dead end, an outage (titles-and-labels 2). Bold.

role-sheet-title.$description: The title of a sheet, and instructions drawn over the live camera — a step below a screen title because a sheet is subordinate to the screen it covers (titles-and-labels 3). Semibold.

role-group-label.$description: A label above a group of rows: regular weight, muted ink, upper case, untracked (titles-and-labels 4).
